findings.reason: CCN26 is accurate across36 nonblank lines with maximum nesting2. This is one preference-form application, not a deeply nested algorithm. Each optional control has its own presence guard and field-specific acceptance rule: model/target/grammar use truthiness, checkboxes preserve explicit false through null checks, grade controls parse and fall back to class/default5, and the legacy override is inferred only when its explicit flag is missing. Grade/range/description/meter publication order also matters to rollback and startup. Existing grade and UI helpers are already reused. A generic field/property setter or options map would relocate these different rules into new machinery; caching every DOM lookup would add local plumbing without removing the rules. No small structural change with a net clarity benefit was identified. Retain the accurate metric, separately from the null checkbox/disabled-state lead below.

findings.reason: CCN26 is accurate across31 nonblank lines with maximum nesting2. The helper performs one synchronous replace-or-move transaction: resolve current/legacy source identity, find the exact original before mutation, preserve same-student position, reserve a retained destination slot for a move, record a source tombstone only when identity/student changes, and save portfolio plus markers atomically through the existing saveWftStudentChange helper. Existing findPortfolioSessionIndex, retainWftStudentSessions and transaction helpers already isolate reusable work. Extracting the source aliases or deletion predicate into one-use wrappers would only move defaults and guards. Combining same-student replacement with the move branch would alter retention/position or tombstone rules. Retain this compact operation and its guards; no useful structural simplification was found.

additional_leads.reason: The defaults are overwritten by supplied null values. With useWordCountTarget:null, line6260 deliberately leaves the existing checkbox unchanged, but line6286 disables the numeric field from !settings.useWordCountTarget. If the checkbox is currently true, the UI can therefore retain an enabled target policy while disabling its editable target field. The normal change listener derives disabled state from the actual checkbox instead. Settings root validation does not reject this nullable field, and mergeWftSettings preserves it, so local saved or loaded settings can reach this path. This is source-supported, not reproduced in this read-only review.

additional_leads.regression_recommendation: After the gate, extend the existing local native preference-integrity scenarios. Start with the actual checkbox checked and an editable target, apply loaded settings containing useWordCountTarget:null, and assert the checkbox/effective target policy and numeric disabled state remain consistent; include an initially unchecked case, explicit true/false and missing field controls, plus failed-save rollback/unknown metadata preservation. Confirm intended null-as-unset behavior before choosing the minimal local fix; do not change broad storage validation or bypass required saves.
